history.period: Established late 1980s; Maha Kumbhabhishekam January 1992; second Kumbhabhishekam 29 April 2002
history.summary: Sri Karthikeya Swamy Temple is the Murugan temple of Chandigarh's Tamil community, located in the Air Force Temple Complex at Sector 31D. During the militancy in Punjab in the 1980s, Tamils in Chandigarh first worshipped a small Vel (spear) on a pedestal, chanting Tiruppugazh bhajanam; after 1990 they built a full temple in Dravidian architecture with a Chola-Pallava style gopuram, designed by Sthapati Rajagopal of Chennai, with idols chiselled by Mahabalipuram sculptors. Shivacharyas from Kanchipuram performed the Maha Kumbhabhishekam in January 1992 and the second Kumbhabhishekam on 29 April 2002; the deity was named 'Lord Karttikeya Swami' by the Maha Swami of the Kanchi Sankara Mutt. The complex also houses sannidhis for Hanuman and the Navagrahas. The temple's own site is murugan.org/temples/chandigarh.htm. CSV state 'Punjab' is imprecise: Chandigarh is a Union Territory.

town_description: Chandigarh is India's first planned city, designed by Le Corbusier, and serves as the shared capital of Punjab and Haryana while being a Union Territory. It is known for the Rock Garden, Sukhna Lake, the Capitol Complex (UNESCO World Heritage), and its grid of leafy sectors. Sector 31D hosts the Air Force Temple Complex in the southern part of the city, where this Tamil Murugan temple stands.
